Initial Setup: Make sure you have the necessary permissions and access to the Azure portal. Connect your Azure subscription to GitHub Enterprise Cloud.
Create OpenShift Cluster: Use the Azure CLI or the Azure portal to create an OpenShift cluster. Specify the required configurations like node count, region, and resource group.
Integrate with GitHub: Set up GitHub Copilot for your project. This includes integrating with Azure DevOps and using GitHub Actions for CI/CD automation.
Development and Deployment: Use GitHub Copilot to write and review code. It can help interpret and document code, as well as suggest fixes and improvements.
Monitoring and Scaling: Use OpenShift's monitoring tools to keep an eye on your applications. Scale your applications as needed based on performance metrics.
Security and Compliance: Configure network policies and access controls to ensure the security of your applications. Keep your applications updated to comply with security standards.
